gaps.gap: R1 Novelty vs NormLift: the plan compares against a weakened NormLift. Tab I lists "NormLift (pixel Kish, beta = 1)" (WF/synth/plan.md:58), and section 1 says the paper still has to prove "view-level evidence with its own epistemic channel" (plan.md:23). NormLift already counts views. Its Sec. 3.3.2 applies Kish "to the per-view rendering weights": N_eff(j) = (sum_v W_j^(v))^2 / sum_v (W_j^(v))^2, where W_j^(v) = sum over the pixels of view v of A_ij (its Eq. 6), which "grows toward the visible-view count". Its Eq. 8 is R(j) = ||f_j|| * N_eff/(N_eff+beta). It also keeps per-view statistics, splits the norm into C_intra x C_inter, and shows in App. E that R(j) rises monotonically with accuracy on ScanNet. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.18898, fetched with `curl -sSL` to WF/reviewer/normlift.html; text in WF/reviewer/normlift.txt. The joint-prior u_ale already equals 1 - R(j) exactly (WF/judge/estim_equiv.log: max diff 0.0). So on static scenes the fixes F1, F2 and F4 rebuild NormLift, apart from a capped view weight. G2 ("AUSE_epi below NormLift") would pass only against the misconfigured row. The fallback F-B title, "calibrated view-level confidence for training-free lifting" (plan.md:126), is NormLift's own abstract claim ("Calibrated by effective multi-view support ... training-free").
gaps.fix:
1. Implement NormLift as its paper defines it: Eq. 6 per-view W_v and f_v, view-level Kish N_eff, Eq. 8 R(j) with beta = 1, and C_intra/C_inter. Use its N_eff (as 1/(1+N_eff)) as its epistemic score. Add a trivial "visible-view count" row for AUSE_epi. About 0.5 pd.
2. In the paper, state that on static scenes the read-out reduces to NormLift's R(j) (m0 = 0, c0 = beta) and to its view weighting. Cite NormLift as concurrent.
3. Delete fallback F-B.
4. Make change handling (C4) the main claim, and make G3 the go/no-go for submission. G2 becomes a parity check, not a claim.

gaps.gap: R3 Calibration is not shown, and the vMF posterior is never used. F6 gives every row the same predictive, p(c) = softmax(beta * mu_p^T t_c), with beta fit on val (plan.md:40). It uses only mu. u_epi, u_ale and kappa never enter it. mu* is the T*alpha-weighted mean (WF/code/formula_checks.log: changing kappa from 10 to 1000 moves mu by at most 4.47e-08). So the ECE and NLL of "Ours" equal those of the averaging row, up to the F1 view weights. The G2 and Tab I test "ECE at most the best deterministic row" cannot be credited to uncertainty. AUSE ranks only, so nothing shows that the u values mean anything in absolute terms. C1 (the conjugate posterior) has no measured effect anywhere in the plan, yet the abstract plan promises "lower ECE".
gaps.fix:
1. Put the posterior into the predictive: p(c) = E over mu ~ vMF(mu*, kappa_post) of softmax(beta * mu^T t_c), approximately softmax(beta * A_d(kappa_post) * mu*^T t_c). Here kappa_post = kappa_hat * n * rbar comes from the F2 joint prior.
2. My check shows this has a real effect where views are few. Command: `python3 WF/reviewer/ad_check.py`, with d = 64 and rbar = 0.85, so kappa_hat = 193.5. Output (WF/reviewer/ad_check.log): A_d = 0.826 at n = 1, 0.909 at n = 2, 0.962 at n = 5, 0.981 at n = 10, 0.996 at n = 50.
3. Ablate three predictives on ECE, NLL and Brier: the plug-in with a global temperature, the posterior predictive, and a 2-parameter beta(u_epi, u_ale) fit on val.
4. Add reliability diagrams and a risk-coverage curve (AURC) for queries that abstain on high u.
5. If the posterior predictive does not beat plug-in + temperature on val, remove "calibrated" from the title and abstract, and call C1 an interpretation, not a method.

gaps.gap:
R4 Math flaw in F3, and it lowers the change signal. F3 centres at read-out (R_c = R - n*zbar), then uses R_c for dispersion and change (plan section 2, F3). Centred vectors are off the unit sphere, so the vMF likelihood and the F2 kappa_hat equation no longer apply. A Gaussian whose observations are all identical gets rbar_c = ||z0 - zbar|| < 1, and that value depends on its class, not on its spread. F2's own check ("one view gives 1/(1+c0)") then fails; it gives ||z0 - zbar||/(1+c0). Measured on CPU with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python3 WF/reviewer/centring_check.py` (MaskCLIP ViT-B-16 laion2b via uags OpenCLIPDense; 7-Scenes chess, office and redkitchen, 8 frames each; log WF/reviewer/centring_check.log):
- Zero-spread content: rbar_c p5/p50/p95 = 0.451 / 0.586 / 0.737. So u_ale (n = 10, c0 = 1) is 0.33 / 0.467 / 0.59 where it should be near 0.
- Static-vs-changed AUROC of 1 - rbar: raw 0.807, plan F3 0.739 (worse), per-pixel centre then renormalise 0.843.
Caveat: "changed" is a random pixel from a far frame of the same scene, not a real rearrangement, and single pixels stand in for Gaussian footprints.
gaps.fix:
1. Accumulate a second channel of centred, renormalised features, z_hat = (z - zbar)/||z - zbar||, with zbar fixed per scene from the mapping frames before accumulation. Compute dispersion, kappa_hat and c from z_hat. Keep raw R for queries.
2. Cost: another N(d+1)*4 B, about 0.26 GB at N = 1M and d = 64 (code report memory model).
3. Add a unit test: identical observations give rbar = 1 for every class.
4. Re-run G1 with this variant, and rewrite the F3 text and its validation.

gaps.gap:

- A render-vs-observation feature residual: 1 - cos between the rendered mu* and the new CLIP feature, lifted to Gaussians with T*alpha. This is the idea behind MIF's discrepancy score (RSS 2026, arXiv 2605.21935; abstract: "A discrepancy detection score is introduced to separate locomotion-induced false-positive changes from persistent changes"; sota report: it includes 1 - cos of features) and CL-Splats' DINOv2 render-vs-real masks. - No published change detector is run with its own code, although 3DGS-CD has code (github.com/520xyxyzq/3DGS-CD, Apache-2.0 per the data report). Whether it runs on sm_120 / torch 2.11 is not checked.
gaps.fix:
